raw:
The user wants Japanese UI text for an EC app:

s1: Message shown on cart screen when cart is empty (there's already a "商品を探す" button at the bottom of the screen)
s2: Title of confirmation dialog for deleting item from cart
s3: Button to execute deletion
s4: Button to cancel deletion

Rules:
- No chatty phrasing
- No questions as labels/titles
- Keep it short
- No unnecessary politeness/explanations
- Don't repeat what the button already says
- No periods at end of labels
- Japanese EC conventions

s1: Empty cart message. Since there's already a "商品を探す" button, the message shouldn't repeat "商品を探しましょう" etc. Something like 「カートには商品がありません」 or 「カートは空です」. Standard EC phrasing: 「カートに商品が入っていません」. But careful: don't explain obvious things... Actually an empty state message is expected. "カートに商品がありません" is standard. Avoid adding "お探しの商品を見つけてください" since button exists. Keep simple: 「カートに商品が入っていません」

Hmm, "カートが空です" vs 「カートに商品がありません」. Either fine. 「カートに商品が入っていません」is common in Japanese EC apps. Period must not end labels/buttons—but s1 is a message, not a label; still, no period needed to be safe. Without punctuation.

s2: Dialog title: 「商品を削除しますか？」— but rule: no question sentences as button or title. So title should not be a question. Titles like 「商品の削除」 or 「削除の確認」. Common non-question title: 「商品を削除します」 sounds like statement. Better: 「商品の削除」. That's clean and standard.

s3: Execute delete button: 「削除する」

s4: Cancel: 「キャンセル」

Output JSON only: {"s1":"...","s2":"...","s3":"...","s4":"..."}</think>{"s1":"カートに商品が入っていません","s2":"商品の削除","s3":"削除する","s4":"キャンセル"}

parsed.s1: カートに商品が入っていません
